newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian official warns over Chechnya recognition.
newsitem.headline: Russian official warns over Chechnya recognition.

text.p: A Russian deputy foreign minister said on Sunday Moscow was ready to break off ties with any country that granted diplomatic recognition to the breakaway Chechen region, Interfax news agency reported.
Viktor Posuvalyuk, speaking on the eve of presidential and parliamentary elections in largely-Moslem Chechnya, described separatism as a dangerous virus.

"We have warned the international community. All governments and foreign policy arms of relevant countries are aware of our categorically negative attitude to potential attempts to recognise Chechnya. So far, there have been no such (attempts)," he told Interfax.
But he said Russia was ready to take severe measures "going as far as the severence of relations".
A foreign ministry spokesman said he was unable to confirm whether Posuvalyuk's comments reflected official Kremlin policy. But, he said, a deputy minister had the right to express his views.
Posuvalyuk did not name any countries but referred to the Middle East.
"It is not for the countries of the Middle East to venture into such games and take part in them, since the spectre of separatism goes beyond the region.

Elections take place in Chechnya on Monday for the presidency of the region, shattered by 21 months of war. Russian troops, sent in to quell the region's push for independence, have withdrawn under a peace deal but Moscow refuses to recognise Chechen independence.
Leading candidates, some of whom advocate a strongly Islamic state structure, agree that international recognition should be one of the main aims of any future Chechen government.
Few countries, however, would be inclined to cross President Boris Yeltsin by formally recognising Chechnya.
